standard.title: Text structure and language feature effectiveness
standard.description: analyse text structures and language features and evaluate their effectiveness in achieving their purpose
standard.prior_knowledge: Students examine how authors adapt and subvert text structures by experimenting with multimodal elements (AC9E9LA03). They have not yet analysed and evaluated the effectiveness of text structures and language features in achieving their purpose.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse text structures and language features and evaluate their effectiveness in achieving their purpose.

nodes.label: Identifying text structures and language features
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the text structure and key language features of a text and describe how they are used.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the main text structure and at least two language features in a provided text and describe their function.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and describe the text structure and a range of language features across at least two text types, explaining how each is used to organise or convey meaning.
wider: Compare how the same text purpose (e.g. review, argument) is structured differently in print versus online environments
Examine how multimodal texts integrate graphics, text and sound, identifying how each mode contributes to the overall structure
Analyse how First Nations Australian authors structure texts that incorporate oral storytelling conventions
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to evaluate the effectiveness of text structures and language features — a judgement that depends on being able to accurately identify and name those structures and features. Without this, evaluation is untethered from the text.

response_modes.reason: Accurate identification of text structures and features requires familiarity with a range of text types; students who have not encountered sufficient examples need practice across contexts before they can evaluate effectiveness.

success_criteria: Identifies the text structure of a provided text by name or description
Names at least two language features and describes their function in the text

nodes.label: Evaluating effectiveness in achieving purpose
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate the effectiveness of text structures and language features in achieving the text's purpose, making a supported judgement.
nodes.minimum_width: Make a supported judgement about whether the text structure and at least one language feature are effective in achieving the text’s purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate the effectiveness of text structures and language features across different sources (e.g. reviews, multimodal texts), making a reasoned judgement with textual evidence.
wider: Compare the effectiveness of the same text transposed between media formats (e.g. print article to online version) and evaluate how the change affects purpose achievement
Evaluate texts from different cultural contexts against their stated purposes, examining how purpose is culturally shaped
Evaluate how documentary or media report structures achieve their purposes through combinations of graphics, text and sound

response_modes.reason: Effectiveness is relative to purpose and audience; students who only evaluate effectiveness in one context may apply a narrow or default standard — multiple contexts build understanding that the same feature may be effective in one context and not another.
Evaluation requires students to hold purpose, feature and audience in mind simultaneously — this reasoning structure needs explicit scaffolding before students can produce independent evaluations.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Evaluating effectiveness opens into rich comparative work across text types, media and purposes — students who engage with multimodal or cross-cultural texts develop a much more nuanced sense of what ‘effective’ means.
success_criteria: Makes a supported judgement about the effectiveness of a text structure in achieving its purpose
Supports the judgement with specific evidence from text structures or language features
